props.title: Murder on the Orient Express
props.initialSlug: Legendary detective hunts killer on snowbound train

sections.content: Sidney Lumet's Murder on the Orient Express sets the gold standard for Agatha Christie adaptations. The film's claustrophobic luxury train setting becomes a pressure cooker of suspicion, with Albert Finney's meticulous Hercule Poirot interrogating an all-star cast including Lauren Bacall, Ingrid Bergman, and Sean Connery. The film's opulent production design and Paul Dehn's sharp screenplay maintain Christie's intricate plotting while adding visual sophistication that influenced later whodunits like Gosford Park (2001) and Knives Out (2019).

sections.content: The success of Murder on the Orient Express launched a wave of lavish Christie adaptations throughout the 1970s and 80s. Death on the Nile (1978) and Evil Under the Sun (1982) continued the formula of exotic locations, period detail, and ensemble casts. These films established a distinct visual language for Christie adaptations: rich production values, methodical pacing, and careful attention to class dynamics among the suspects. This influence extends to modern interpretations like Kenneth Branagh's Murder on the Orient Express and Death on the Nile (2022).

The 1974 film's approach to Poirot himself became definitive. Albert Finney's portrayal emphasizes the detective's theatrical flourishes and moral certainty, while maintaining the character's essential humanity. This balance influenced later Poirots like David Suchet in the long-running television series (1989-2013) and established how future adaptations would handle Christie's beloved detective. SUBHEAD: The Art of the Drawing Room Mystery

movies.title: And Then There Were None
movies.slug: Ten strangers are lured to an island where they're murdered one by one, in this atmospheric adaptation of Christie's darkest mystery.

sections.content: Murder on the Orient Express perfected the "drawing room mystery" format, where suspects are confined in an elegant setting. The film's innovative use of flashbacks and careful blocking in cramped train compartments influenced later confined-space mysteries like Identity (2003) and Bad Times at the El Royale (2018). Cinematographer Geoffrey Unsworth's work in capturing both the train's luxury and claustrophobia created a template for how to film confined mysteries with style and tension.
